description:
Surfaced by the bedrock-287 audit.

`State.health` is consumed in exactly two places, both matching `:ok` literally: `do_wait_for_healthy/2` (impl.ex:236) and `notify_waiting_for_healthy/1` (impl.ex:309). It is never returned by any `handle_call` in foreman/server.ex, never logged, never emitted as telemetry.

So the three non-`:ok` verdicts — `:starting`, `:unknown`, `{:failed_to_start, :at_least_one_failed_to_start}` — are computed and then discarded. The distinction between 'still booting' and 'a worker is wedged' exists in the code and reaches nobody.

That is why bedrock-287 (order-dependent fold) and bedrock-mxt (never recomputed at boot) could both persist unnoticed: nothing reads the value closely enough to notice it was wrong. Fixing the computation without giving it a reader means it can silently re-rot.

Note `wait_for_healthy/2` itself currently has no production callers either (checked lib, test, bedrock_ex); only guides/deep-dives/architecture/infrastructure/foreman.md:111,229 claims recovery uses it.

## Options

- emit telemetry on every health transition (the codebase has established tracing modules per component)
- log transitions at info/warning, so a wedged worker is visible in the log without a subscriber
- return health from a `handle_call`, so an operator can ask
- or decide the value is genuinely unused and delete it along with `wait_for_healthy/2` — a smaller surface is better than one nobody reads

Prefer one of the first three if recovery is ever meant to gate on foreman readiness; prefer the last if it is not.
title: Foreman health is computed but never exposed, so no operator or supervisor can read it
